To draw a regular hexagon having a $40\text{ mm}$ side in two different orientations:

**(a) Vertical Orientation (Two sides horizontal):**
1. Draw a horizontal baseline.
2. Construct a circle or vertical centerline of appropriate diameter, or use a $30^\circ-60^\circ$ set square.
3. Draw top and bottom horizontal sides of length $40\text{ mm}$ parallel to each other.
4. Draw the remaining four inclined sides at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal to complete the regular hexagon.

**(b) Horizontal Orientation (Two sides vertical):**
1. Draw a vertical centerline.
2. Draw left and right vertical sides of length $40\text{ mm}$ parallel to each other.
3. Complete the top and bottom angled boundaries using $30^\circ$ or $60^\circ$ set squares meeting at sharp vertex points on the vertical axis.
proTip: For a regular hexagon of side $S$, the distance across corners is $2S$ and the distance across flats is $2S \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Use this to cross-verify dimensions.
